description: Evrosion supersession registry required by R-010.21. It records supersessions that accepted canonical sources have already declared. It creates none: an entry that cannot cite an accepted declaring source does not belong here. Published technical editions retain clause identities and requirements; the source map records actual edition hashes and original source lineage. This registry describes how earlier wording resolves.

rules.authority: Each entry's authority comes from the cited declaring sources, never from this file. Unresolved or unaccepted resolutions belong in the explicit proposal process, not here.
rules.scope: A narrow amendment changes only the stated scope. Everything else in the affected source remains in force.
rules.history: Superseded technical requirements remain identifiable. Public edition content is checked against architecture/plans/source-map.json; source lineage is recorded separately.
rules.kind_vocabulary_status: rename, narrow-amendment, clarification, full-supersession, deprecation and historical-alias are the kinds the owner's reconciliation directive requires. extension and finalization are proposed in the explicit proposal process and await acceptance.

kinds.rename: Same concept, new name; the old name becomes a historical alias.
kinds.narrow-amendment: One clause, reading or scope changes; the rest of the source stands.
kinds.extension: Obligations are added; the original clause is unchanged.
kinds.clarification: Meaning is confirmed where the text could be misread; no behaviour changes.
kinds.finalization: A later passage of the same document settles an earlier provisional status.
kinds.deprecation: Still valid for a declared window, with a named replacement.
kinds.historical-alias: An old identifier or label maps to the current one.

effective_status.WITHDRAWN: The declaring source was itself superseded; kept for history.

entries.scope: Name and file extension of the single native Evrosion package format.
entries.effective_rule: Use .zion in living documentation, code, tests and examples. .sion in older imports names the same format. Never implement two formats, and never add .sion compatibility because an old plan contains the old spelling.
entries.reason: The owner renamed the format after the E-series was written; R-008 and R-010 record it as a naming migration, not a second format.

authority.statement: That name has been superseded by the user's later decision: .sion -> .zion. This is a naming migration, not two package formats.

Current canonical extension: .zion. Older archived docs may retain .sion with clear supersession annotation. Do not create compatibility for .sion solely because an old planning document contains the old spelling.

entries.old: Any reading of E-025.80 ('Compatibility Comes Later') and E-025.118 as making supported Windows compatibility optional for the eventual ordinary-user product
entries.new: E-025.80 and E-025.118 govern early implementation ordering only. Ordinary-user releases must bundle an operational Windows Compatibility Runtime for their declared supported software (ADR-0003.WINDOWS).
entries.scope: The ordinary-user release obligation only. Early staging, native-platform prerequisites, M0-M5 and the 0.1 developer-preview gate are unchanged.
entries.effective_rule: Windows compatibility stays out of M0-M5 and 0.1, and is required, bundled and activated on demand for ordinary-user releases.
entries.reason: The owner accepted a product amendment making out-of-box Windows compatibility part of user-facing releases.

authority.statement: E-025.80 and E-025.118 still govern early staging. Any reading of 'later' as 'optional forever for the ordinary-user product' is superseded by this ADR.

authority.section: Roadmap / Documentation Amendment, required changes 4, 6 and 7
authority.statement: Change Windows compatibility language from purely optional/later ecosystem work to staged during early developer milestones and built-in first-class infrastructure for user-facing releases. Do not silently alter the current M0 completion criteria. Do not force either feature into Evrosion 0.1.

entries.notes: Accepted is not implemented: the Windows runtime is DEFERRED and no compatibility engine is selected.

entries.old: Possible reading that bundling a Windows runtime (SUP-005) requires it to run alongside native software
entries.new: E-022.1 on-demand activation and native independence remain binding. A bundled provider can stay inactive while only native apps run.
entries.scope: Activation and dependency model of the bundled compatibility runtime.
entries.effective_rule: Ship the provider; activate foreign services on demand; native apps never depend on it or pay for it (INV-EVO-004).
entries.reason: Prevents SUP-005 from being read as overturning E-022.1.

authority.statement: Bundling does not require always-running foreign services or foreign kernel policy. E-022.1's on-demand activation remains binding.
E-022.1's native independence and on-demand activation remain unchanged. A bundled provider can remain inactive while only native apps are running.

entries.old: E-010, E-012.25 and E-019 durable-state, reinstall-without-wipe and lifecycle rules, which did not address migration from a foreign OS
entries.new: The same rules also cover preservation-first migration from a foreign OS: journaled, verified, resumable, retaining the source until health checks pass and the owner explicitly authorizes reclamation (ADR-0003.MIGRATION).
entries.scope: Adds Migration Source State and migration obligations. No existing durable-state rule is weakened or replaced.
entries.effective_rule: System Generations, Durable User State and Migration Source State stay distinct; destructive reclamation needs explicit owner authority.
entries.reason: The owner accepted a product amendment requiring data-preserving installation.

authority.statement: E-012.25's reinstall-without-wipe and E-010/E-019 durable-state rules are extended to foreign-OS migration, not replaced.
Data preservation extends the existing E-010/E-012/E-019 lifecycle rules. No kernel invariant, stable ABI, compatibility engine or journal format changed.

entries.old: ADR-0014 permanent retention of closed authority-domain slots and unreachable lineage nodes
entries.new: ADR-0029 explicit generation-safe domain reuse and bounded unreachable-lineage collection
entries.scope: Internal authority-domain and lineage metadata only. Object descriptors, scheduler identities, physical resources and original M1 evidence are unchanged.
entries.effective_rule: Use checked domain generations and preserve all handle-reachable ancestry during explicit collection. No implicit process/resource reclamation or detached raw-node token may bypass these requirements.
entries.reason: Repeated M2 authority binding must not permanently consume empty domains and unreachable lineage; naive reuse would revive stale identities or sever revocation.

authority.statement: supersedes ADR-0014's permanent retention of closed authority-domain slots and unreachable lineage nodes only
You may choose a better mechanism than an older proposal if the behavioral guarantees remain intact.

entries.history_preserved: ADR-0014 and imported plan requirements remain identifiable; the public edition does not revise historical M0/M1 evidence.

entries.new: ADR-0030 atomically revoked group of pinned per-object branches
entries.scope: Internal lineage representation only; all-descendant invalidation, sealed custody, one ACTIVE incarnation and quiescence-before-replacement guarantees unchanged.
entries.effective_rule: Pin each per-object revocation branch with a private generation-checked handle; validate and revoke the entire group under the exclusive Authority borrow before replacement.
entries.reason: Existing lineage nodes each belong to one object. Private branches preserve verified lookup/collection semantics without destroying permanent roots or caching reusable node indices.

authority.statement: refines the single incarnation revocation node
You may choose a better mechanism than an older proposal if the behavioral guarantees remain intact.

entries.reason: Sustained service restart must not exhaust metadata or alias old authority and execution identities.
